canonicalIngredients.name: beef mince
observations: 1/2 lb lean, plus 1/2 lb Italian sausage (s1)
500 g veal mince + 500 g pork mince in place of beef (s2)

canonicalIngredients.name: mozzarella
observations: 4 cups shredded total: 1.5 in cheese mix + 2.5 topping (s1)

causalSequence: soften onion in oil (plus garlic s0/s1; plus carrot celery soffritto s2)
add tomato base (+ paste, stock, herbs per source); simmer covered
simmer 15-20 min (s0), 5 min (s1), or 2 h adding water as it dries (s2)
if using: make bechamel - melt butter, whisk in flour, add milk gradually, season salt nutmeg (s2)
if using: mix ricotta, egg, parsley, mozzarella, parmesan, salt (s1)
boil dried noodles al dente first (s1); fresh sheets go in raw (s0, s2)
grease dish; thin sauce layer on base
layer sheets, sauce, cheese layer (mozzarella s0 / ricotta mix s1 / cheeses + bechamel s2); repeat 3-6 layers
finish with sauce and cheese on top
bake 180 C ~30-40 min (s0) or covered then uncovered to brown (s1: 45+15 min at 350 F; s2: 20+10 min)
techniqueFacts: cheese layer diverges by tradition: plain mozzarella (s0), ricotta-egg mixture (s1), bechamel plus provolone and mozzarella (s2)
two sources bake covered with foil then uncover to brown the cheese top
all three rest the baked lasagne before slicing (5-15 min); one allows up to 45 min
fresh sheets need no pre-boil (2 sources); dried noodles are boiled al dente and rinsed cold (1 source)
sauce simmer time is the flavour lever: 15-20 min weeknight versions vs 2 h traditional ragu
one source deliberately omits garlic from the ragu to keep the Bolognese flavour soft
one source reduces the sauce well before layering so the lasagne is not soggy
one source starts every layer with sauce on the dish base to prevent sticking
